* 
 The Police-Inspector of Basavanagudi Women P.S. has filed chargesheet against Accused No.1 to 3 for the offences punishable U/s. 498A, 506 r/w/s 34 of IPC. & Sec.3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. The criminal law has been set into motion based on the first information statement of Smt.Sumitra.K. (Suma).
The gist of the prosecution case is that CW-1 married Accused No.1 on 30-05- 2019.
At the time of marriage, the accused No.1 to 4 have demanded and taken Rs.Five Lakhs cash and gold ornaments weighing 100 gms. as dowry from complainant and her parents.
The accused No.1 to 4 caused physical and mental cruelty to CW1 for giving birth to a female child.
The accused No.1 used to quarrel with CW-1 for petty matters and the accused No.2 to 4 used to tell that they will get the accused No.1 to get marry for second time and demanded divorce from CW1.

When the accused No.1 was residing separately along with CW-1 accused used to quarrel with her and to drop her in the house and went to the house of other accused and when CW-1 came to the house, the accused No.1 to 4 used to quarrel with CW-1, assault her and gave life threat to her and Smt Sumitra K vs Balaraju S on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196447130/
2 thus tortured CW-1 both by physically and mentally in demand of additional dowry.
Based on the said information, a case in Cr.No.163/2023 came to be registered against the accused for the aforesaid offences.
3. After completion of the investigation, the P.I of Basavanagudi Women P.S. has filed chargesheet against accused for the aforesaid offences.
On receipt of charge sheet, this court took cognizance of the alleged offences.
Pursuant to the issuance and service of summons, accused entered appearance and were enlarged on bail.

The prosecution papers was furnished to the accused as required U/s.207 of Cr.P.C.

Before framing charge an opportunity of being heard was provided to the accused and after hearing them and the prosecution and as there was sufficient materials, the charge for the aforesaid offences was framed and same was read over to the accused in the language known to them, to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
The plea of the accused was recorded.
Thereafter, the matter was set down for prosecution evidence.
5. In order to prove the charges, the prosecution has examined PW-1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.3 documents.

As there was no any incriminating evidence appearing against the accused, the recording of Statement of Accused as required U/s.
313 of Cr.P.C., was dispensed with.
6. Heard arguments on both the sides.

sentences.text:
7. The following points arise for my determination:-
 1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable  doubt that the accused persons caused physical and  mental cruelty to the complainant in demand of dowry  and threatened her and thereby accused have committed  the offences punishable U/s.498A, 506 r/w/s 34 of IPC.
 & Sec.3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
 2) what order?
 5  C.C.No.20165/2024  8.

My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1 ........In the Negative.
 Point No.2........

As per final order, for the following:
 REASONS  9.
POINT No.1 :- It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

In order to bring home the guilt of the accused,
the prosecution has examined one witness as PW-1 got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P3 documents.
Ex.P1 is the first information statement.
Ex.P.2 is the Panchaname.
Ex.P.3 is the further statement of complainant.
10. CW-1 was examined as PW-1 Smt. Sumithra.

She in her examination-in-chief has deposed that her marriage with accused No.1 was performed on 30-05-2019 and deposed after the marriage, accused looked after her well and deposed accused did not subjected her to any physical and mental cruelty, in demand of dowry and deposed accused did not abused and Smt Sumitra K vs Balaraju S on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196447130/
4 threatened her.
PW-1 deposed that there was petty quarrel between her and accused in respect to family issues, for which she  6  C.C.No.20165/2024 went to the police station.
There the police have took her signatures on documents.
PW-1 identified Ex.P.1 first information statement and also identified her signature at Ex.P1.
PW-1 also identified Ex.P.2 spot Panchanama and her signature at Ex.P2 and she pleaded her ignorance about the contents of Ex.P.1 and P.2.
The learned Sr.APP treated PW-1 as hostile witness and cross examined her.
During which PW-1 admitted that she and accused have compromised the matter and denied all other suggestions.
11. On appreciation of entire materials on record, it is apparent that PW-1 being the informant, key and material witness have turned hostile to the prosecution case.
Therefore, this court was pleased to reject the prayer of the learned Sr.APP to summon other chargesheeted witnesses.

Even, if the summons was issued to other chargesheeted witnesses, no purpose would be served as the material witness has given go-bye to her own statement and also the valuable time of the court would be saved.
As such other charge sheeted witnesses were dropped and prosecution evidence was taken as closed.
In view of the material witness, turning hostile the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused  7  C.C.No.20165/2024 beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

POINT No.2:-

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
In exercise of power conferred Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., Accused No.1 to 4 are acquitted of the offences punishable U/s. 498A, 506 r/w/s 34 of IPC. & Sec.3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The bail bonds of accused No.1 to 4 shall be in force for a period of 6 months.
